fields.description:
## Context

Make the bridge execution path portable across local shells, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI,
and bare environments without breaking checked-out workflows or environments that still use the
legacy reconcile vocabulary. The current production workflow contains about 185 lines of runner
logic, and `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shells out to `gh workflow disable/enable` without a
repository argument. That best-effort GitHub-only schedule control silently disappears outside GHA.

The bridge/reconciler execution path is otherwise CI-neutral. The repository as a whole is not:
`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py` intentionally reads `GITHUB_TOKEN`, hard-codes the GitHub mirror, and
calls `api.github.com`; `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` and `usage_report.py` optionally write
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Those are GitHub-specific mirror-health/reporting features, not bridge
execution, and are documented out of scope rather than used as evidence of bridge portability.

The parent epic makes GitLab a required portability proof even though this repository is not
currently hosted there. Ship a thin committed `.gitlab-ci.yml` as a contract artifact over the same
runner-neutral entrypoint. Vendor GitLab's own Draft-07 schema from
`gitlab-org/gitlab/app/assets/javascripts/editor/schema/ci.json` at commit
`776c20ad5675eecea0c2010433a94d98d745e921`; the immutable raw URL is
`https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/776c20ad5675eecea0c2010433a94d98d745e921/app/assets/javascripts/editor/schema/ci.json`
and its observed SHA-256 is `7568b544b4b95102f21e9fd89d769d54ee6f86b35d2fbb7f7b947d6fa9fc4dda`.
This is the GitLab-owned source documented by GitLab, not the distinct SchemaStore mirror. Validate
it offline with the existing Draft-07-capable `jsonschema` dependency; record the source URL,
revision, retrieval date, dialect, and checksum in an adjacent provenance file. The GitLab artifact
is exercised structurally and through its extracted shell body rather than by standing up a shared
runner.

## Runner-neutral entrypoint

Create `scripts/run_reconcile_bridge.py` as the one executable bridge wrapper. It selects only the
canonical `rebar bridge preview` or `rebar bridge sync` operation, owns the canonical wrapper
contract (`CANONICAL_EXIT_CODES`, required environment names, and a 60-minute/3600-second timeout),
rejects shallow clones, and contains no GitHub/Jenkins/GitLab branch.
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and local documentation
invoke that exact file. Provider wrappers retain only checkout, credentials, timeout,
artifact/masking syntax, and the platform-specific expression that maps the entrypoint exit status
to job success/failure. Each provider timeout is derived from or contract-checked against the
runner's 3600-second constant rather than copied as an unchecked value.

The entrypoint calls the checkout build and canonical bridge route. Legacy `rebar reconcile --mode`
and direct-engine routes remain untouched, including their 3/4/75 results, so older workflow
revisions and environments continue to run during migration.

`scripts/run_reconcile_bridge.py` is the wrapper source of truth for the secret-name set and timeout.
Its allowed exits are derived and cross-checked against
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py::_Disposition`, whose canonical column is 0/1/2.
Contract tests import the runner constants, parse all three provider wrappers, and compare their
exit-code table, secret-name set, and timeout; the tests do not restate a second table.

## Portable destructive-repair control

Replace the `gh workflow disable/enable` helpers with the durable control already shipped by story
`1104`: `refs/reconciler/gate` pause documents written through
`rebar_reconciler._ref_lock.set_pause` and cleared through the lower-level observed-OID
`release(..., oid=observed_oid)` CAS seam, using the same configured remote and identity behavior as
`rebar bridge pause/resume`. Both `fsck --repair` and the peer `doctor --repair` destructive path use
the same repair-owned pause context around their existing lock check and mutation. This preserves
both command surfaces while closing the provider-neutral schedule race; a scheduled pass on GitHub,
Jenkins, or GitLab reads the gate before mutation and exits benignly while paused.

The repair sequence is explicit and fail-closed:

1. Read the durable gate. If another actor already paused the bridge, abort the repair and do not
   clear that pause. Otherwise generate a repair-unique reason/token, CAS-write it, and set a local
   `pause_created` flag only after the CAS succeeds. Any transport, authentication, corruption, or
   CAS uncertainty aborts the destructive repair.
2. Run the existing provider-neutral `_reconciler_in_flight` check against
   `refs/reconciler/lock`. HELD, corrupt, timeout, or indeterminate aborts the repair.
3. Run the repair.
4. In `finally`, clear only when `pause_created` is true. Read the validated pause document and its
   OID as one snapshot, verify its reason equals this repair's unique token, then call
   `_ref_lock.release(..., oid=observed_oid)` so the reason check and deletion are bound to that exact
   OID. A mismatch or CAS miss means the pause changed/was replaced: do not retry against a fresh OID
   and surface the condition. A foreign or changed pause is never cleared; a clear failure leaves the
   bridge paused for operator recovery rather than silently reopening it. Do not use `clear_gate`
   here because its internal ref reread would reopen the ownership-check TOCTOU window.

The lock remains the in-flight safety check; the durable gate is the schedule pause. This preserves
the currently-working GitHub safety behavior without a provider API and closes the Jenkins/GitLab
race.

## Verification strategy

- Run the real entrypoint in temporary repositories with vendor variables scrubbed and with
  representative local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments. Results and
  repository/ref postconditions must be identical, and `gh` is absent from `PATH`.
- Use a bare git remote to set the durable pause, attempt a canonical sync, and prove the pass exits
  benignly without mutation. Exercise pause write failure, pre-existing foreign pause,
  corrupt/indeterminate lock, ownership change before clear, and resume failure and prove destructive
  repair fails closed without clearing another actor's pause. Drive both `fsck --repair` and
  `doctor --repair` through this shared safety contract.
- Create a real shallow clone (or drive `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` to `true`) and assert
  the entrypoint exits non-zero with the named `f193` error before any bridge operation runs.
- Parse the production GHA, Jenkins, and GitLab wrappers and execute their extracted shell bodies.
  The Jenkins `sh` body is a single-quoted Groovy string so secrets reach the shell/masking layer
  without GString interpolation. Validate `.gitlab-ci.yml` offline with the existing `jsonschema`
  dependency against the vendored official schema and verify its provenance metadata/checksum.
- `shellcheck` is a pinned CI/dev prerequisite installed by the verification workflow. The contract
  test hard-fails with a setup error when the binary is missing; it never skips. Shellcheck runs over
  the script bodies extracted from all three configs, and a malformed wrapper/config fixture must
  make extraction, schema validation, or lint fail.
- The production GHA workflow is still the scheduled artifact rebar runs, so the shared entrypoint is
  exercised by the existing 20-minute schedule. No Jenkins or GitLab controller is stood up: both
  committed configs use the same extracted-body, offline-schema, and contract checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/run_reconcile_bridge.py` is the one runner-neutral bridge entrypoint.
- [ ] GHA, Jenkins, and GitLab wrappers contain only checkout, credentials, timeout,
      masking/artifacts, and exit mapping.
- [ ] Checked-out legacy workflows and old-vocabulary environments retain the legacy reconcile
      commands, defaults, messages, and 3/4/75 behavior.
- [ ] `fsck --repair` uses the durable pause ref plus the fail-closed lock check and requires no `gh`
      binary.
- [ ] `doctor --repair` uses the same repair-owned pause context; pause/lock/resume uncertainty never
      permits either destructive repair to proceed silently.
- [ ] A real bare-remote test proves the durable pause blocks canonical sync identically from local,
      GHA-shaped, Jenkins-shaped, and GitLab-shaped environments; an existing foreign pause is never
      cleared, and only a repair-owned unique pause may be cleared by CAS.
- [ ] A five-environment contract matrix runs the real entrypoint under scrubbed
      local/GHA/Jenkins/GitLab/bare environments, with `gh` absent, and asserts identical
      exit/output/ref effects and no vendor-variable reads.
- [ ] A shallow-clone test drives the true shallow condition and asserts the named `f193` error and
      non-zero exit before reconciliation.
- [ ] The shipped GHA artifact invokes the shared entrypoint and remains the workflow exercised on
      the existing schedule; committed `Jenkinsfile` and `.gitlab-ci.yml` artifacts invoke the same
      entrypoint.
- [ ] All three provider configs are cross-checked against the runner constants and `_Disposition`
      for one exit-code table, one secret-name set, and the 60-minute timeout, never against
      duplicated unchecked tables.
- [ ] `.gitlab-ci.yml` validates offline against GitLab's Draft-07
      `app/assets/javascripts/editor/schema/ci.json` pinned at commit `776c20ad...`; its immutable
      source URL, revision, retrieval date, dialect, and observed SHA-256 are committed and verified.
- [ ] Jenkins shell bodies are single-quoted; pinned `shellcheck` runs over extracted script bodies
      from all three configs in CI, fails when unavailable, and rejects malformed extracted
      script/config fixtures.
- [ ] GitHub-only mirror/report helpers are documented as out of bridge-execution scope.

## File impact

- `scripts/run_reconcile_bridge.py`: runner-neutral entrypoint and wrapper contract.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: thin production GHA wrapper.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: install pinned shellcheck for contract verification.
- `Jenkinsfile`: thin committed Jenkins wrapper with safe credentials.
- `.gitlab-ci.yml`: thin committed GitLab wrapper over the shared entrypoint.
- `.github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json` and `.github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.provenance.json`:
  pinned official schema plus source URL, revision, retrieval date, and checksum for offline
  validation.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`: durable repair-owned pause plus fail-closed lock safety
  without `gh`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`: preserve `doctor --repair` while routing its destructive mutation
  through the same durable repair-owned pause context.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py`: update string-based
  monkeypatches of the removed `_reconciler_pause`/`_reconciler_resume` helpers and retain held-out
  safety coverage.
- focused workflow/runner/fsck tests: five-environment parity, three-config schema/contract/shell
  validation, shallow rejection, and pause ownership/lock/resume fail-closed behavior.
- `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/release-notes.md`: local/GHA/Jenkins/GitLab usage, legacy continuity,
  and GitHub-specific known gaps.
